topic: Relational databases and simple SELECT queries
title: Your first SQL query
instructions:
## A database of students

The database has three tables: **students** (id, name, programme, level, hometown), **courses** (code, title, credits, lecturer) and **enrolments** (student_id, course_code, semester, mark). Marks can be NULL when a result is not yet in. Use the Tables panel to peek at the data.

A **query** asks the database a question. The starting query asks for everything in the students table. Press **Run** and look at the rows.

## Do this

Change the query so it returns only the **name** and **programme** of students at **level 100**, sorted by name (A to Z). Three rows should come back.

The pattern is:

```sql
SELECT column1, column2 FROM table WHERE condition ORDER BY column1;
```

config.schema:
CREATE TABLE students (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  programme TEXT NOT NULL,
  level INTEGER NOT NULL,
  hometown TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE courses (
  code TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  title TEXT NOT NULL,
  credits INTEGER NOT NULL,
  lecturer TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE enrolments (
  student_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES students(id),
  course_code TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES courses(code),
  semester TEXT NOT NULL,
  mark INTEGER,
  PRIMARY KEY (student_id, course_code, semester)
);

checks.label: The query returns the names and programmes of level 100 students, in name order
checks.expectedQuery: SELECT name, programme FROM students WHERE level = 100 ORDER BY name

checks.label: It filters with WHERE
checks.message: Use WHERE to keep only level 100 students.

realityNote: A real university registry holds hundreds of thousands of rows across dozens of tables, but the question is asked in exactly the same way.
